of $52,000. We renegotiate supplier contracts annually to secure bulk discounts, better pricing, and more favorable delivery terms. Additionally, we regularly solicit bids from multiple vendors. However, it is very important to highlight and understand that LCPS operates in a region with a limited pool of available food and supply vendors.

We are a very large, spread-out operation and receive limited bidders able to meet our needs when we do put out solicitations. Related to vendor contracts and in support of sustainability initiatives, one recent example for this school year is our bulk milk pilot program at Riverside High School.

This program is aimed to increase milk consumption by high school students while also reducing program expenditures. This program provides reusable cups for students to self-serve milk at a dispensing unit versus the traditional carton of milk.

This pilot has seen positive results so far with increased milk consumption and reduced expenses by lowering the per unit cost of milk and minimizing waste associated with the individual cartons. We also continue to focus on reducing food waste from monitoring the inventory turnover reports to ensure minimal spoilage to growing our food recovery program.

The school nutrition team closely watches all aspects in this area. We are especially proud of our food recovery program by rescuing edible food and reallocating it to school inventories, pantries, and local food banks. So those are some of the examples where efforts are focused to help reduce expenditures with the overall financial objective to balance expenditures with available resources. And that concludes my presentation on those other remaining funds and I'd be happy to take any questions.
